The finding: our renders are 4–15× too coarse

measured

The protocol specifies a 140 mm field. How many pixels that is depends entirely on the render's pixel spacing — and every corpus we have with a spacing field sits far to the coarse side of what an image intensifier actually produces.

A YOLO detector trained at 1024 px was being asked to find vertebrae in a 93-pixel frame. That was the worry. It was worth measuring rather than believing.

The ladder — and the worry is wrong

Real films, the film-trained detector, coarsened by a factor. One corpus, one detector, everything else held, so only pixel size varies. A factor of 3 on a film is about ctsp_drr's spacing; 6 is about ts_drr's.

downsample≈ corpusfield pxrecall @0.05recall @0.25dup/body
1×native film83699.14%98.71%6.87%
2×—41899.15%99.15%6.41%
3×ctsp_drr / verse_drr27999.57%99.14%6.44%
6×ts_drr13999.14%98.28%7.73%
Flat. 836 px to 139 px costs 0.00 points of per-vertebra recall. Vertebral bodies are large, low-frequency objects and the detector does not need the pixels. So “detection is the binding constraint at ~60 points” stands as published, the re-render is not the main event, and the C2 failure needs a different explanation — most likely the render-trained detector itself, at 0.740 recall against the film detector's 0.991.

One prior result pointed the other way — a paired test moved detection +6.4% at 6.25× the pixels — but that was measured on naming panels, not on sweep fields, and on a different task. On this task, at this scale, the effect is zero.

Image formation, calibrated on real fluoroscopy

366 pairs · 6 specimens · overnight

You asked whether the CT→fluoro map could be learned from DeepFluoro and applied to the whole spine. The literature said no (paired diffusion +7.5 mm worse at low confidence; pix2pix hallucinated geometry; CycleGAN nothing). The residual said the same thing more precisely: after exact geometry, the physics and nine device terms, what is left is a smooth per-frame field with nothing local in it — 0.4% of variance at ≤2 px — so there is nothing for a regional network to learn. So it was calibrated, not learned, and it transfers to whole-spine CTs because every fitted term belongs to the device.

Geometry: exact, and tested

Convention settled by reprojecting 14 shipped 3-D landmarks into the 14 shipped 2-D ones: 0.00 px median and p90 over 111 frames, and on all six specimens. Volume is (z,y,x); ext @ inv(cam-to-pelvis-vol); the extrinsic was required and not guessable.

What the physics already explains

80.9% of a real frame's attenuation variance (NCC 0.899), same band shape in every specimen: r = 0.75 at bone scale, falling below 2 px (halo, blur, noise) and above 16 px (a vignette with one sign in 89% of frames; a heel gradient that flips with the rotation flag).

Nine device terms, leave-one-specimen-out

Held-out gain median +4.1 (−3.1…+8.0). Stable across folds: receptor blur 0.81 px, halo width 3.06 px, vignette −0.133, heel +0.045. Fit on near-AP, test on the most lateral frames (≥15°, max 36.5°): +4.6. Beyond 36.5° DeepFluoro has no frames.

The ceiling, and where the rest lives

Only 0.3–0.5% of variance is stochastic → ceiling 99.5%. A per-frame quadratic surface (window, scatter, heel; no image content) takes physics to 92.3% and the calibrated model to 93.9%. Bands ≤8 px are at the floor; the six remaining points are at 8 px and coarser.

The bowel question, settled by eye

Inside the field the raw DRR carries 1.03–1.05× the real frame's bowel-scale energy at r 0.92–0.95 — the bowel is right. What makes a frame read as fluoroscopy is crisp cortical edges and grain, which the calibrated frames now have. The calibrated model is over-smooth at 8–32 px (its free scatter blur): next term to constrain.

The follow-up fits, six minutes each

Scatter width boxed to 6–16 px: +4.3, 15.8 px with spread 0.4, every term stable — the calibration now applied. Scatter dropped: +4.1 but receptor blur destabilises. kb opened to 6: runs to 3.0 and the held-out gain falls to +3.5, so the 2.5 bound stays.

Your angle regression, measured

Nine terms fitted inside three tilt bins (≤8°, 8–15°, ≥15°) and scored against the global terms on the same held-out frames: +0.0, −0.2, −0.4 points. Per-angle terms buy nothing within the 36.5° the data span; the identified terms move by less than their fold spread. The terms are applied unchanged.

The photon budget, fitted

The count at which the model's quantum draw — now placed after scatter and before receptor blur, where the detector counts it — reproduces the real fine-band grain: median 2,918 per 0.78 mm pixel, p10–p90 773–4,767. The assumed 4,000 was the 79th percentile; the builder's old range put half its draws above anything the device produces.

Not done, on purpose

No diffusion or pix2pix model. DeepFluoro not extended. No volume grafted. The DRR process is calibrated and applied to continuous whole-spine CTs: TotalSegmentator, 156 of 1939 with C2 and sacrum. VerSe turned out regional (1 of 120 masks spans C2→lumbar).

A whole-spine CT under a real C-arm pose, calibrated

T9→L5 on the detector, every box projected from its mask, nothing annotated; the scanner table stripped (TotalSegmentator's whole-body scans include it); the rotation flag honoured so orientation matches the stored real frames. Under the most lateral real pose (36.5°) it renders T10→L5 the same way.

Now running, three arms: a two-class detector (vertebra, sacrum) trained on calibrated synthetic frames from 48 clean whole-spine subjects under the five training specimens' real poses — physics alone / plus mild randomisation / plus the aggressive film tier — each tested on the held-out specimen's 111 real frames: sacrum recall, anchor-called rate, vertebra-region hit. The first per-vertebra recall on real fluoroscopy anyone will have measured. Measured: see the section below.

Manuscript: Methods, Results, Discussion, abstract and two figures; 7,244 words declared and measured; builds clean at 35 pages. Cited: Grupp 2020, Unberath 2019, Gao 2023, Rapuri 2026, Dhont 2020.

Looked at before training, and it was wrong

The first synthetic set (left sheet; the two real frames are top-left). Stripes and blotches from the aggressive randomisation tier, and featureless white and black frames from zero-count pixels clipping to an attenuation of 13.8 and wrecking the window. No number the build printed showed any of it. Rendered again with a detector black level, no randomisation and the real writer's window rule (right sheet): bone bright, fine grain, crisp cortex, the sacrum box (green) on the sacrum, vertebra boxes (red) on the spine.

The first per-vertebra recall on real fluoroscopy

trained on calibrated synthetic only · tested on DeepFluoro's real frames

A two-class detector (vertebra, sacrum) trained on 597 calibrated synthetic frames — 48 whole-spine subjects under 14 real poses, every box projected, nothing annotated — once per held-out specimen, reaches mAP50 0.91–0.97 on synthetic validation and finds the sacrum on 76.9% of 365 real frames pooled over all six specimens (by specimen 47.8–96.2%), calling a sacrum on 98% of frames with 0.64 false sacra per frame. That is the honest number. It is far from counting-grade, and it is the first such number anyone has measured.

The seed control, which bounds everything else

Three training seeds of one dataset on one specimen: 51.4, 77.5, 56.8%. Twenty-six points from the seed alone. So the single-seed arms on that specimen — mild randomisation 55.0/30.6, the aggressive tier 47.7/53.2, three times the subjects 47.7, both 58.6 — do not differ from each other by more than the seed does. Remedies can only be ranked with seeds averaged and specimens as folds; tools/deepfluoro_anchor_report.py prints the spread beside every mean.

The trap the drawn calls exposed

The first scores were ~40%. Drawn on the frames, the truth boxes sat at the bottom of some fields: 160 of 366 real frames are stored upside down (rot-180-for-up), the synthetic frames were all turned up, and the real test frames had been written as stored. A third of 17-1882 was inverted pelves the detector had never seen. Fixed in the writer; every trained arm re-scored on the corrected frames without retraining. No printed number showed it.

Where the rest goes, and gaps to state

The sacrum is found in the upright anteroposterior frames; the oblique frames, where the lumbosacral region saturates, collect clusters of low-confidence vertebra calls on the saturated region (the renderer has no exposure control, so oblique synthetic views were slabs too). DeepFluoro's specimens are cadaveric pelves with air around them; the training anatomy is living abdomens that fill the field.

The C2 arm, and why its number is void

2593 walks

The cranial detector did finish training: 60/60 epochs, over 934 held-out images and 23,092 instances. So the answer to “I thought I trained one?” is yes — the earlier job built the corpus and died on a missing package, printing its DONE marker a second later.

0.23% overall. 8.1% of those that reached.

Three theories, all killed by measurement

  • Detector confusing C1 for C2 — no. Its C2 box lands on C2 in 218/219 renders, on C1 zero times.
  • Ground-truth indexing error — no. Under --anchor-by class the chain index comes from the detector's own box and is self-consistent.
  • Field a shade too tight above C2 — not the main term.
The detector finds C2 on 99.5% of full renders and 31% of 93-pixel sweep frames. C2 is inside the frame at all on only 15%. That gap is the answer.

On the grid

ipcai_2020_full_res_data.zip2541.6 MB
ipcai_2020_ds_8x.zip41.9 MB
ipcai_2020_ds_16x.zip10.7 MB

366 real fluoroscopic X-rays over 6 cadaveric specimens, each with a 1 mm isotropic CT, per-image pose, a full-resolution 2-D segmentation and 14 landmarks.

The 3-D segmentation has seven classes: left- and right-hemipelvis, vertebrae, upper-sacrum, left- and right-femur, lower-sacrum. The vertebrae label spans 90–112 mm — about 2–3 lumbar levels, merged into one class rather than labelled per level.

All 14 landmarks are pelvic: FH, GSN, IOF, MOF, SPS, IPS, ASIS. Not one is spinal.

How it got unblocked

The JHU archive returned 403 to curl, wget and urllib — from the grid, from your workstation, over http and https, and with a complete browser header set. Not the IP, not the headers: the TLS fingerprint.

A client presenting Chrome's fingerprint is served normally. curl_cffi with impersonate="chrome" worked first try. No browser needed, so the phone was never necessary.

The pose convention, read not guessed — and verified to 0.00 px

Each projection carries gt-poses/cam-to-pelvis-vol, a 4×4 in millimetres, camera→volume — invert it to project. Also cam-to-left-femur-vol and the right, each with a good-fov flag.

Images and segmentations are 1536×1536 at 0.194 mm/px: squarely in the C-arm band, and 7.7× finer than ts_drr.

What this is really for. It cannot test counting — there are never 8–12 bodies in frame. But it carries a sacrum, which is the caudal anchor the whole protocol hangs on, on 366 real fluoroscopic images with exact geometry. And because it pairs real images with the CT and the pose that made them, it is the one corpus that can calibrate the renderer against real fluoroscopy, pixel for pixel — replacing the present validation target, which is FluoroCap's top decile by grain.

Known ceiling: the same 366-image / 6-specimen Siemens CIOS Fusion corpus SyntheX and the 2026 diffusion paper already used — about 6 mm landmark error, Dice 0.86, for hip structures.

Do not read the ablation off this table. Every arm's validation set is degraded the same way as its own training set, so each is graded on its own distribution — in-domain validation cannot show a domain-transfer effect. Only dr_eval can, and it is queued behind all five. Epoch counts are uneven from node contention; the slowest needs ~20 more hours.

What the literature settled

107 agents, adversarially verified

Three levers, measured on real images

Simulation fidelity — naive DRR → DeepDRR moves real-image landmark error 78.2 → 24.7 mm, with ~68% from polyenergetic multi-material attenuation alone. Already in your renderer.

Strong domain randomization — 6.44 mm with zero real training images against 6.46 for a real-trained control, on 366 real cadaveric C-arm images. The lever you had not pulled; now built and training.

Scale — 1k → 10k renders: 6.61 → 5.95 mm.

Refuted — do not build this

CycleGAN scored 6.62 mm and ADDA 6.41 against 6.44 for no adaptation at all. Indistinguishable, point estimate worse, and both require real fluoroscopy at training time.

So the DRR→fluoro GAN is measured and buys nothing. It was not built.

Also withdrawn: the planned Pelphix citation. Its 99.2→71.7 is surgical-phase accuracy, not detection. The 0.03-point agreement was a coincidence between two different quantities and would not have survived review.

The honest ceiling

No published system detects and names vertebrae from real intraoperative fluoroscopic content at counting-grade recall. No per-vertebra recall on real fluoroscopy is published at all.

LevelCheck's 100% imports identity from the patient's own prior CT by registration. The DeepDRR/SyntheX line reports millimetres and discards low-belief landmarks without stating the fraction.

Your 71.67% has no peer. That is a hazard and an opening.

Errors caught, not shipped

the unglamorous half
  • A silent holdout failure. Freeing 260 GB deleted five crop banks that ~90 scripts named as --holdout-bank. An unreadable bank left the trained-on set empty and the evaluation ran over cases the model was fitted on, without raising — an error that only ever flatters. tools/holdout.py raises now.
  • The augmentation washing films to blank white. The self-check passed on a noiseless phantom while real radiographs were being destroyed.
  • The gate written to prevent that then passed “blown white” 12 times out of 12, because it was global. It now measures saturation and measures structure only where the source had structure.
  • Three contamination checks that all erred toward clean. ts_drr reported at 0% when it is 84.3%.
  • My own analysis tool using the wrong axis — box elements 0 and 2 instead of 1 and 3. Verified: 100% monotonic against the named cervical order on the correct pair, 43% on the wrong one.

Every one of these produced a plausible number. That is the project's named failure mode and it is why the render gets looked at.

Decision on the table

yours

1 · Re-render at C-arm resolution

The direct fix. ~0.3 mm/px with a spacing field, so a 140 mm field is ~470 px. Unblocks the C2 arm and every future detection-on-sweep number.

Cost: a render job. Disk: the corpora grow ~25× in pixels.

2 · Price the resolution term first running

A ladder on real films with the good detector: downsample 1×/2×/3×/6× and measure per-vertebra recall at each. 3× on a film is about ts_drr's spacing.

This says whether resolution is a side-quest or the main event — before spending the render.
